goal:
Design the v3 top-level lexicon package (DOCS ONLY this pass; no code/port yet). Deliver two artifacts: (1) a lexicon inventory ledger mapping every legacy src/slop/lexicon primitive and the 7 lexical rules to a 4-way partition (PORT-TO-LEXICON / MOVE-TO-RULES / CROSS-CUTTING / DROP-OR-DEFER); (2) a 'Lexicon Subsystem' section in DESIGN.md mirroring the AST Subsystem.

Settled principles: Boundary = general linguistic concept vs slop-invented metric. Lexicon owns ONLY the linguistic kernel (tokenize, curated stop-words, type/token counts, hapax ratio, frequency+Zipf distribution, alphabet/coverage/overlap set-ops, and reusable algorithms FCA + collocations + single-swap affix clustering), named in lexicographic language. Slop's named metrics/batteries/verdicts live at a higher layer (TBD, possibly under linter). Litmus: lexicon must be usable OUTSIDE the linter; imports nothing from component/rules/linter. Interface = stream of plain (text:str, role:Role, span:Span); Role is a lexicon-owned enum (MODULE/PACKAGE/CLASS/CALLABLE/PARAMETER/BODY_REF), not ComponentKind; no AST node types cross the boundary. Bridge = ast grows Node.identifiers()->Iterator[(str,Span)] (option A); component layer wires it + unions fs names; dissolves the two legacy direct AST walks (view.body_token_locations, stutter). Span extracted from ast/ to a shared base both ast and lexicon depend on. Zero new runtime deps: keep hand-rolled FCA + Zipf-OLS + collocations + single-swap affix; decline rapidfuzz (op is single-swap not general Levenshtein) and concepts lib (MIT but 2020-stale); stop-words = curated code list (Newman-14), injectable. Naming discipline: rename slop coinages in kernel (packets->collocations, etc.).

Defer (not this pass): cross-view batteries (imposters/slackers + vocabulary displacement = rules joining lexicon+structure by Span); diagnostic/ harness; concept-escape (corpus-blocked); Ronin abbreviation splitting (optional future).

summary.title: Lexicon Subsystem design (docs only): charter, (text,role,span) interface, inventory ledger
summary.what: Authored the 'Lexicon Subsystem' design for v3: a top-level lexicon/ package owning ONLY the linguistic kernel (tokenize, curated stop-words, frequency/hapax/Zipf distribution, alphabet/coverage/overlap set-ops, FCA, collocations, single-swap affix clustering), named in lexicographic terms and usable outside the linter. Defined the (text, role, span) interface with a lexicon-owned Role enum, the option-A ast.Node.identifiers() bridge, Span extraction to a shared base, cross-view batteries as Span-joins, and a zero-new-deps posture. Delivered a 4-way inventory ledger (PORT / MOVE-TO-RULES / CROSS-CUT / DEFER) over every legacy src/slop/lexicon primitive and the 7 lexical rules. Docs reorganized into docs/.internal/design/LEXICON.md (ledger appended); added a convention-blind casing note. No source or tests changed.
summary.why: Legacy lexical capability is sprawled across view.py + affix/clusters/actions/profile/diagnostic, mixing token measurement with AST walks and rule policy -- the same disease the AST subsystem cured. One owner with a hard 'linguistic concept vs slop coinage' boundary makes vocabulary a standalone library and keeps slop's invented metrics/verdicts out of the kernel.

decisions.chose: General linguistic concept -> lexicon; slop-invented metric/threshold/battery -> higher rule layer.
decisions.rationale: Litmus: would a corpus linguist recognize it independent of slop, and is it usable outside the linter. Keeps slop coinages out of the kernel.

decisions.chose: Stream of plain (text:str, role:Role, span:Span); Role is a lexicon-owned enum, not component.ComponentKind.
decisions.rationale: No AST node type crosses the boundary; importing ComponentKind would couple lexicon upward.

decisions.chose: Option A: ast grows Node.identifiers()->Iterator[(str,Span)]; component layer tags Role and unions fs-derived names.
decisions.rationale: Pure navigation+text+span is within the AST charter; dissolves the only two legacy direct AST walks (view.body_token_locations, stutter).

decisions.chose: Extract Span from ast/ to a top-level shared base both ast/ and lexicon/ depend on.
decisions.rationale: Span was never an AST type; keeping it in ast/ would force lexicon -> ast and break the peer relationship.

decisions.chose: Zero new deps: hand-rolled FCA, Zipf-OLS, collocations, single-swap affix; curated code stop-word list.
decisions.rationale: The kernel is code-specific, not natural-language; surveyed libs are stale, prose-oriented, or solve a more general problem than slop has.

decisions.chose: Consumer-driven: foundation + stand up lexicon/ + port distribution to enrich the live vocabulary rule; defer collocations/affix/FCA until their rule is built.
decisions.rationale: v3 rule layer has only 3 rules; full kernel port up front would be unconsumed, unvalidated code.

rejected.reason: The op is a single-substitution check on equal-length token tuples, not general Levenshtein; already optimal hand-rolled.
MIT but maintenance-stale (2020); a working string-pure compute_concepts already exists.
Prose-oriented; suppresses identifier-common words and misses SE boilerplate -- actively hurts.

rejected.alternative: Case enum / binding to a language's casing convention
rejected.reason: Tokenizer is convention-blind and case is normalized away before measurement; convention violation is style, not structural debt.

review_notes: Docs-only intent; no source or tests changed. Implementation is tracked under a separate follow-on intent.

Mainline store is drift-damaged: base_commit d6a80bd over-derives the prepared diff to the whole-branch (500 files). The fingerprint below is hand-narrowed to this intent's real footprint (the design doc); fingerprint confidence lowered to reflect the override.

architectural_claims: lexicon/ is a bottom-layer peer of ast/, importing nothing from component/rules/linter; usable outside the linter.
Span is the substrate source-location primitive (not an AST type) and moves to a shared base shared by ast/ and lexicon/.
Cross-view batteries (imposters/slackers, vocabulary displacement) are rules joining lexicon+structure by Span, not lexicon members.
migration_notes: Next pass (consumer-driven): extract Span to shared base; add ast.Node.identifiers(); stand up lexicon/ (roles/stopwords/tokenize/corpus); re-point build_lexicon bridge; prove vocabulary byte-identical; then port distribution (Zipf/narrate).
